claim_verdicts.source: Chrome 153 headless via CDP, reviewer scratch run on git show stage-0:www/*.html served from 127.0.0.1:8099; no HTML/MDN docs root in versions.yaml, none under refs/
claim_verdicts.evidence: T2: two buttons added to index.html; handler 1 sets h1 text then busy-waits 3 s; button 2 clicked 0.5 s later. Page log: `h1 start 836`, `h1 end 3835`, `rAF (render step) 3838`, `h2 start 3839`. The second click was queued, not lost, and its handler started only after the first returned: one task at a time, each to completion. Observed in Chrome only; the single 'queue' is the simplification depth_notes allow.

claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: scripts/up.sh:12; refs/flutter-website sites/docs/src/content/perf/isolates.md 'Web platforms and compute'; pub.dev/packages/http (1.6.0)
claim_verdicts.evidence: up.sh:12 `(cd DonHang.App && flutter build web >/dev/null)`. isolates.md: "Dart web platforms, including Flutter web, don't support isolates." ... "The compute() method runs the computation on the main thread on the web". pub.dev http (r1 fetch): "By default, package:http uses BrowserClient on the web". So the app's Dart runs on the page's main thread and its requests go through the browser.

The click was queued, handled after the loop, and the link opened ~18 ms late.

issues.quote: Picks the next waiting task and runs it before any other
issues.text: q1 option a (key) lost the run-to-completion part: 'runs it before any other' reads as priority over other tasks, not 'lets it finish before starting another'. Still the only defensible option, so the key stands; the wording is weaker than §3/§4 and explanation.correct ('each to completion').
issues.fix: Option a en: "Picks the next waiting task and lets it finish before starting another"; vi: "Chọn task đang chờ tiếp theo và để nó chạy xong rồi mới bắt đầu task khác".

issues.quote: The browser has many threads for its own work, but a page's handlers run on one thread
issues.text: q2 explanation.correct (en and vi 'Trình duyệt có nhiều thread cho việc riêng của nó') still asserts 'many threads', the wording r1 rephrased out of claim 4 and §6 as unsupportable. Key c remains correct.
issues.fix: en: "The browser does some work outside the page's thread, but a page's handlers run on one thread; a second click waits until the first handler returns." vi: "Trình duyệt làm một số việc bên ngoài thread của trang, nhưng handler của trang chạy trên một thread; cú bấm thứ hai chờ tới khi handler đầu trả về."

issues.quote: Two click handlers never run at the same moment; the second waits in the queue until the first has finished.
issues.text: 'handler' / 'click handler' / 'event handler' is not in known_vocab and not in Core concepts, yet it carries §4, §6, q1, q2, q3 and q5. From context I guess it means 'the JavaScript that runs when something is clicked', but nothing says so, and the Core concepts talk about 'a click to handle' without naming the code that does it.
issues.fix: In the task queue line of Core concepts, add one plain sentence: "The piece of JavaScript that runs for a click is called that click's handler." (plain word, no bold).

issues.quote: the same way async/await in C# hands the thread back during I/O.
issues.text: 'I/O' is an acronym I have not been taught; the threads lesson summary talks about 'waiting for a file, a network reply or a database', never 'I/O'. This is the sentence that links the new idea to what I already know, so it should not hinge on an unknown word.
issues.fix: Replace 'during I/O' with 'while it waits for a file or a network reply'.

issues.quote: Fetching data with JS pauses the whole page until the data arrives, the way a synchronous call would.
issues.text: 'synchronous' is not in known_vocab or Core concepts. The misconception compares to it, and q4's explanation for option b uses 'a synchronous wait on the page's thread' to explain why the option is wrong, so I cannot follow either comparison.
issues.fix: Replace 'the way a synchronous call would' with 'the way a call that holds the thread until it gets its answer would'; in q4 explanation b, replace 'a synchronous wait on the page's thread' with 'a wait that held the page's thread'.

issues.quote: clicks on their links go straight to the browser, which loads the next address. There is nothing on them that could freeze.
issues.text: §5 tells me link clicks on the lab pages go straight to the browser and nothing there can freeze. §7 then freezes index.html and expects the link not to open. I cannot reconstruct the missing step: why does a link click, which 'goes straight to the browser', wait behind the page's thread? And the lesson never says that code typed in the Console runs on the page's thread.
issues.fix: Replace the §5 sentences with: 'the pages hold no JavaScript of their own, so nothing on them runs long enough to freeze; a click still passes through the page's thread first.' In §7 step 1, add: 'Code typed in the Console runs on the page's thread.'

issues.quote: Depending on the browser, that means the link opens late, or the click is handled as if it had just happened.
issues.text: I cannot tell these two outcomes apart, so I do not know which one I saw. The Expected result also stops at 'the page responds again' and does not say whether the link I clicked will open afterwards, which is exactly what the question asks.
issues.fix: In Expected result, add what happens to the clicked link after the loop ends; in the Suggested answer, keep one outcome and drop 'or the click is handled as if it had just happened'.

issues.quote: On a shop's page, you click "Calculate total".
issues.text: The situation is a generic shop page, not a moment in Đơn Hàng; §5 later says the lab pages have no JavaScript, so this button does not exist in the system I know. The question at the end is answered well by §4, so it still works.
issues.fix: Anchor the scene to Đơn Hàng in one phrase, e.g. 'On an order page like the one the Đơn Hàng app will have, you click "Calculate total".'

issues.quote: Takes the next queued piece of a page's JavaScript and runs it to the end
issues.text: q1: the correct option is a near-verbatim copy of the event loop definition in Core concepts ('takes the next waiting piece of a page's JavaScript from a queue and runs it') and is also the longest option, so I can pick it by matching words.
issues.fix: Reword option a in other words (e.g. 'Picks one waiting task and lets it finish before starting another') and bring the other options to similar length.

issues.quote: An instant reply would matter only when the connection were fast, but the scenario states a slow one
issues.text: q4 explanation c talks about connection speed, but option c is about the server being on the same machine. The link between the two is not clear to me and makes me doubt my reasoning. Explanation b also says 'the app awaits the reply', but the lesson never told me the app's code uses await.
issues.fix: Explanation c: 'Where the server runs does not matter here: even a slow reply leaves the page usable, because the browser does the waiting.' Explanation b: replace 'the app awaits the reply and' with 'the app hands the request to the browser and'.
